name: Japanese kumi-daiko (modern taiko ensemble)
lineage: Japanese modern-concert taiko-ensemble (kumi-daiko) tradition codified 1951-onward by Daihachi Oguchi (Osuwa Daiko, Suwa city, Nagano prefecture) as a deliberate-modernization of older village-festival matsuri-and-shrine taiko-percussion. The canonical concert-ensemble: nagado-daiko medium-barrel-drums, odaiko large-barrel-drum (typically center-stage spectacle-instrument), shime-daiko small-tightly-tensioned drum (rhythmic-keeper), chappa hand-cymbals, and atarigane small-bell. Choreographed-and-virtuosic ensemble-staging differentiates concert-taiko from the older communal-festival-taiko. The 1970s-1980s rise of touring-troupes (Kodo on Sado-island, Ondekoza precursor, San Jose Taiko in North-America) made kumi-daiko a global Japanese-cultural ambassador and seeded an international Japanese-diaspora taiko-community.
